course.title: Barbing
course.tagline: Cut clean fades, shape-ups and styles with clippers and skill, and finish your first paying client.

days.title: Welcome to Barbing
days.goal: By the end of today you can explain and practise: Your kit is clippers, trimmers, guards 0 to 8, a comb, scissors, a cape and a spray bottle.

video.title: How to Fade Hair the Easy Way

steps: Get your tools ready: clipper with guards, trimmer and foil shaver.
Watch the video. It explains the main point in simple steps: A clipper guard number equals one-eighth of an inch of hair left behind.
Your kit is clippers, trimmers, guards 0 to 8, a comb, scissors, a cape and a spray bottle. Go slowly. Practise on a model or a practice head.
Do the same move three times. Check your work in a mirror or a photo after each try.
Write down what went well, what was hard, and one thing to do better tomorrow.
days.task: Practise welcome to barbing on a model or a practice head. Your kit is clippers, trimmers, guards 0 to 8, a comb, scissors, a cape and a spray bottle. Take a photo of your work.
days.challenge: Do welcome to barbing two times today. Make the second try neater than the first.

quiz.q: What does a clipper guard number tell you?
options: How much hair the guard leaves behind
How long the haircut will take
quiz.explain: A higher guard number leaves more hair behind. A number 1 guard leaves about one-eighth of an inch.

quiz.q: Which tool do you need most for a fade?
quiz.explain: A clipper with guards is the main tool for fading. You change guards to blend the hair from short to long.

quiz.q: What should you always do between clients?
options: Cut hair without putting a cape on the client
Use the same cape without shaking it out
quiz.explain: Always disinfect your clippers between clients. Clean tools keep every client safe.

days.title: Know Your Tools
days.goal: By the end of today you can explain and practise: Learn each clipper, trimmer, foil shaver, comb and shear, and what job each one does.

video.title: How to Fade Hair for Beginners

steps: Get your tools ready: clipper with guards, trimmer and foil shaver.
Watch the video. It explains the main point in simple steps: A foil shaver cuts hair closest to the skin for a clean skin finish.
Learn each clipper, trimmer, foil shaver, comb and shear, and what job each one does. Go slowly. Practise on a model or a practice head.
Do the same move three times. Check your work in a mirror or a photo after each try.
Write down what went well, what was hard, and one thing to do better tomorrow.
days.task: Practise know your tools on a model or a practice head. Learn each clipper, trimmer, foil shaver, comb and shear, and what job each one does. Take a photo of your work.
days.challenge: Do know your tools two times today. Make the second try neater than the first.

quiz.q: What does a foil shaver do?
options: It cuts hair closest to the skin for a clean skin finish
It dries the hair with hot air
It combs the hair into place
It sprays water on the hair
quiz.explain: A foil shaver cuts hair closest to the skin for a clean skin finish.

quiz.q: Which tool cleans up sharp edges and lines?
quiz.explain: The trimmer is the tool for sharp edges and clean lines.

quiz.q: What must you check before you start cutting?
options: If the client has cuts or broken skin
If the client likes loud music
If the shop door is open
quiz.explain: Always check the client for cuts before starting. Never cut broken skin.

days.title: Hygiene and Safety
days.goal: By the end of today you can explain and practise: Disinfect blades with clipper spray, wipe tools with Barbicide, and never cut broken skin.

video.title: Anybody Can Fade

steps: Get your tools ready: clipper with guards, trimmer and foil shaver.
Watch the video. It explains the main point in simple steps: Clipper blades must be disinfected between every client.
Disinfect blades with clipper spray, wipe tools with disinfectant, and never cut broken skin. Go slowly. Practise on a model or a practice head.
Do the same move three times. Check your work in a mirror or a photo after each try.
Write down what went well, what was hard, and one thing to do better tomorrow.
days.task: Practise hygiene and safety on a model or a practice head. Disinfect blades with clipper spray, wipe tools with disinfectant, and never cut broken skin. Take a photo of your work.
days.challenge: Do hygiene and safety two times today. Make the second try neater than the first.

quiz.q: How often must you disinfect clipper blades?
quiz.explain: Clipper blades must be disinfected between every client.

quiz.q: Which one do you use to kill germs on clipper blades?
quiz.explain: Clipper spray kills germs on blades and keeps every client safe.

quiz.q: What should you do with your tools after each client?
quiz.explain: Wipe tools with disinfectant after each client. Clean tools keep every client safe.

days.title: Holding the Clipper
days.goal: By the end of today you can explain and practise: Grip the clipper firmly, thumb on top, and practise steady upward strokes on a mannequin head.

video.title: Basic Clipper Cutting

steps: Get your tools ready: clipper with guards, trimmer and foil shaver.
Watch the video. It explains the main point in simple steps: Cut the opposite way the hair grows for an even cut.
Grip the clipper firmly, thumb on top, and practise steady upward strokes on a practice head. Go slowly. Practise on a model or a practice head.
Do the same move three times. Check your work in a mirror or a photo after each try.
Write down what went well, what was hard, and one thing to do better tomorrow.
days.task: Practise holding the clipper on a model or a practice head. Grip the clipper firmly, thumb on top, and practise steady upward strokes on a practice head. Take a photo of your work.
days.challenge: Do holding the clipper two times today. Make the second try neater than the first.

quiz.q: Which way should you cut for an even cut?
options: Cut the opposite way the hair grows
Cut the same way the hair grows
Cut only from the top down
quiz.explain: Cut the opposite way the hair grows for an even cut.

quiz.q: Which tool do you hold when you practise steady upward strokes?
quiz.explain: You hold the clipper firmly, thumb on top, for steady upward strokes.

quiz.q: What should you do after each try with the clipper?
options: Check your work in a mirror
quiz.explain: Check your work in a mirror or a photo after each try so the cut stays even.

days.title: Clipper Guards Explained
days.goal: By the end of today you can explain and practise: Guard 1 leaves 3mm, guard 2 leaves 6mm, guard 4 leaves 13mm; start long, go shorter.

video.title: How to Put Guards on Clippers

steps: Get your tools ready: clipper with guards, trimmer and foil shaver.
Watch the video. It explains the main point in simple steps: Guard 2 leaves about 6mm of hair.
Guard 1 leaves 3mm, guard 2 leaves 6mm, guard 4 leaves 13mm; start long, go shorter. Go slowly. Practise on a model or a practice head.
Do the same move three times. Check your work in a mirror or a photo after each try.
Write down what went well, what was hard, and one thing to do better tomorrow.
days.task: Practise clipper guards explained on a model or a practice head. Guard 1 leaves 3mm, guard 2 leaves 6mm, guard 4 leaves 13mm; start long, go shorter. Take a photo of your work.
days.challenge: Do clipper guards explained two times today. Make the second try neater than the first.

quiz.q: How much hair does a guard 2 leave behind?
quiz.explain: Guard 2 leaves about 6mm of hair.

quiz.q: Which tool controls how much hair is left behind?
quiz.explain: Clipper guards control the length. A higher guard leaves more hair behind.

quiz.q: Which guard should you start with?
quiz.explain: Start long, then go shorter. You can always cut more off, but you cannot put hair back.

video.title: How to do a PERFECT fade! Easy steps

Watch the video. It explains the main point in simple steps: Sectioning keeps each area of the cut even and controlled.
Part the head into top, sides and back with clips so each zone is cut cleanly. Go slowly. Practise on a model or a practice head.
Do the same move three times. Check your work in a mirror or a photo after each try.
Write down what went well, what was hard, and one thing to do better tomorrow.
days.task: Practise sectioning the head on a model or a practice head. Part the head into top, sides and back with clips so each zone is cut cleanly. Take a photo of your work.
days.challenge: Do sectioning the head two times today. Make the second try neater than the first.

quiz.q: Why do you section the head before cutting?
options: Sectioning keeps each area of the cut even and controlled
It makes the cut take longer
quiz.explain: Sectioning keeps each area of the cut even and controlled.

quiz.q: Which tool holds the hair in sections while you cut?
quiz.explain: Hair clips hold each section in place so every zone is cut cleanly.

quiz.q: What should you do before you start cutting a section?
options: Clip the other sections out of the way
quiz.explain: Clip each section out of the way so you cut one clean zone at a time.

days.title: The All-Over Buzz Cut

Watch the video. It explains the main point in simple steps: A buzz cut uses one guard length over the whole head.
One guard all over, steady strokes, then clean the neckline and edges. Go slowly. Practise on a model or a practice head.
Do the same move three times. Check your work in a mirror or a photo after each try.
Write down what went well, what was hard, and one thing to do better tomorrow.
days.task: Practise the all-over buzz cut on a model or a practice head. One guard all over, steady strokes, then clean the neckline and edges. Take a photo of your work.
days.challenge: Do the all-over buzz cut two times today. Make the second try neater than the first.

quiz.q: What is an all-over buzz cut?
options: One guard length over the whole head
A different guard on every part
A cut done with scissors only
quiz.explain: A buzz cut uses one guard length over the whole head.

quiz.q: Which tool do you use for a buzz cut?
quiz.explain: A buzz cut is done with clippers and one guard over the whole head.

quiz.q: What should you clean after a buzz cut?
quiz.explain: After a buzz cut, clean the neckline and edges so the cut looks sharp.

project.title: Week 1 Project: The All-Over Buzz Cut
project.brief: Practise everything from week 1: One guard all over, steady strokes, then clean the neckline and edges. Show the finished work and ask for feedback.

Work slowly and check your work as you go

quiz.q: What should you do if the guideline is not straight?

days.title: Skin Fade Technique

Watch the video. It explains the main point in simple steps: A skin fade goes right down to bare skin at the bottom.
Use a foil shaver below the bald line, then blend 0, 0.5 and 1 guards upward. Go slowly. Practise on a model or a practice head.
Do the same move three times. Check your work in a mirror or a photo after each try.
Write down what went well, what was hard, and one thing to do better tomorrow.

quiz.q: How far down does a skin fade go?

quiz.q: Which tool shaves below the zero line in a skin fade?

quiz.q: What should you check after a skin fade?
options: That the skin is smooth with no nicks
That the hair is long on top
quiz.explain: Check the skin is smooth and clean after a skin fade, with no nicks or red marks.
